reason: Refutation failed on every axis. mediaAccess.ts:82-87 is a bare catch-all around the whole authorization body that logs and returns true; it is reached only AFTER the token path (line 69) and the !user deny (line 79) are bypassed, so during a DB fault an ANONYMOUS request holding only a key is granted a private project's media. There is no second gate: server.ts:227-248 (authorizeMediaRequest) is the sole authorization for /hls-public, /hls-proxy, /video-raw and /video-proxy, server.ts has zero addHook/preHandler/onRequest (grep across src/ finds addHook only in a test), and callers cannot distinguish allowed from could-not-determine because the function returns a bare boolean. Blast radius survives a DB outage: after the gate the routes serve bytes from disk (safeLocalPath + createReadStream, server.ts:375-444) or from an R2 fetch (server.ts:337) with no further DB read, so the request path does NOT die earlier. The project-id sub-claim is also correct: keys are minted as videos/${projectId}/${randomUUID()} (VideoGenerationService.ts:293) and the full key is embedded in every player URL (LocalStorageAdapter.ts:64, R2StorageAdapter.ts:94 and :322), so every viewer of a public/unlisted project receives the owning project id. Held at P2 rather than P1 on two genuine mitigations found while trying to refute: the catch is not attacker-triggerable (resolveProjectForKey is UUID_RE-guarded and Drizzle-parameterized, and postgres.js max:10 queues rather than throws on pool saturation, so an attacker cannot induce the fault), and exploitation additionally requires prior possession of an unguessable double-UUID key. Note the /health 503-on-db-down drain (server.ts:204-213) is NOT a real mitigation here: it probes SELECT 1, which stays green under the statement-timeout/transient-error conditions that trip this catch.
evidence: Read mediaAccess.ts in full (catch at :82, logger.error+return true at :85-86); read server.ts:200-495; grep canServeMediaKey -> only server.ts:239 and :244; grep addHook|preHandler|onRequest over src/ -> only rawBodyRouteConfig.test.ts:96; grep videos/${projectId} -> VideoGenerationService.ts:293; read db/index.ts:28-32 (max:10, connect_timeout:10); no test in src/**/__tests__ references authorizeMediaRequest or canServeMediaKey, so nothing pins deny-on-error; git log -L 82,87 shows the block introduced deliberately in 1838bbf with an availability-bias comment.

reason: Every refutation avenue failed. (1) No verification guard exists on the path: firebase-auth.ts read in full (1-112) has no email_verified/emailVerified check, and a repo-wide grep for email_verified|emailVerified returns ZERO source hits -- the only matches are inside the reviewer's own findings/security.md. There is no blocking function either (grep beforeCreate|beforeSignIn|sendEmailVerification across client-web, admin-web and backend-api/src = no hits), so decoded.email is simply whatever string the account was registered with and Firebase makes no ownership guarantee about it when email_verified is false. (2) Reachability holds even though I found the signup helper is dead UI code: signUpWithEmail (client-web/lib/firebase.ts:131) is referenced ONLY by its own context wiring and three test mocks -- no client-web component calls it, and UserProfileButton.tsx:13 / PaywallOverlay.tsx:27 offer Google sign-in only. That does NOT save it, because the Email/Password provider is demonstrably ENABLED on the project: admin-web ships a live email+password login form (admin-web/components/LoginPage.tsx:7 and :18 calling signInWithEmailAndPassword) against the same NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* config (admin-web/lib/firebase.ts:16-26 identical to client-web/lib/firebase.ts:22-29), and the backend verifies against a single project (services/firebase.ts:8-21). With that provider on, accounts:signUp is reachable directly over the Identity Toolkit REST API using the public web API key that ships in the client bundle -- no UI button required. (3) There is no second authorization step: the invite grants edit immediately. editableProject/projectEditableWhere (collabAccess.ts:43-51, 81-83) is the ONLY gate on ~30 mutating routes (projects.controller.ts:143-394, sections.controller.ts:183-695, markers, editor-state, share, permalink), and it ORs created_by with collaboratorExists. (4) The reviewer's cited line is in fact too NARROW, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding: collabAccess.ts:28-33 and :118-123 match `eq(collaborators.invited_email, user.email.toLowerCase())` on every request, so access is granted by raw email match whether or not the claim at firebase-auth.ts:77-86 ever ran, and firebase-auth.ts:50 refreshes dbUser.email from the token on every login of an existing user. Gating only line 77, as the finding's fix proposes, would therefore NOT close the hole -- collabAccess must be fixed too. (5) Severity stays P1, not P0: the invite never expires (schema.ts:745-759 has no expires_at, no token, no single-use flag -- only owner/self revocation at collaborators.controller.ts:145), so the window is indefinite, but the attacker needs a specific pending invitee's address AND that address must have no existing Firebase account (signUp fails EMAIL_EXISTS otherwise), and the prize is edit on one project, not tenant-wide compromise. Pre-signup invites are the designed normal state (schema.ts:742-744; controller line 110 stores user_id NULL; listRows marks them status pending at :50), so the vulnerable window is routine, not exotic.

reason: Every link of the chain survived attack. (1) No guard: markFailed's only predicates are eq(billing_transactions.id, opts.transactionId) at BillingService.ts:229 and eq(stripe_payment_intent_id, opts.paymentIntentId) at :235 -- no status term, no prior SELECT, and the set is an unconditional {status:'failed', error}. The codebase knows the pattern it is missing: RevisionService.markFailed takes an expectedStatus and throws 'illegal revision transition' (revisionService.test.ts:240); billing simply omits it. (2) The two events DO hit the same row: createCheckoutSession stamps payment_intent_data.metadata.transactionId = tx.id (:161) alongside session metadata.transactionId = tx.id (:162), so the failure path (stripe-webhook.controller.ts:42 reads pi.metadata.transactionId) and the success path (grantFromSession:194 reads session.metadata.transactionId) resolve to the SAME billing_transactions row by primary key. The fallback branch is no safer -- grantFromSession writes stripe_payment_intent_id onto the succeeded row (:208), so a metadata-less failed event still finds the succeeded row by PI id. Under Stripe Checkout a declined card leaves the session open on the same PaymentIntent and the buyer retries to success, so fail-then-succeed on one PI is the ordinary path; corruption needs only the failed event to be PROCESSED after the success, which Stripe's at-least-once, order-not-guaranteed delivery plus the 500 retry makes routine rather than exotic. (3) Earnings claim verified: billing.controller.ts:155 filters and(creator_user_id=me, status='succeeded'), so the flipped row vanishes from salesCount, totalGrossCents, totalNetCents and recent; admin/v1/billing.controller.ts:15-26 filters t.status==='succeeded' for totalVolume, totalPlatformFees, activeCreators, activeBuyers and totalTransactions. (4) Access is a SEPARATE grant, so 'silently keeps access' is right: hasAccess reads user_purchases (:94-101), UNIQUE(user_id, content_type, content_id) at 024_billing.sql:53, and markFailed never touches user_purchases -- the buyer keeps watching while the sale disappears from the books, which is exactly why nobody notices. (5) The 500 is real: stripe-webhook.controller.ts:57-59 catches any handler throw and returns reply.code(500), which Stripe treats as a failed delivery and redelivers with backoff for up to 3 days. (6) No test: services/billing/__tests__ contains only grantFromSession.test.ts, which covers success idempotency and never exercises markFailed or event ordering. Reachability holds -- registerStripeWebhookRoutes is registered unconditionally at server.ts:571 with no feature flag. Held at P1 rather than P0: the sole self-healing path is accidental (reconcileCheckout -> grantFromSession early-returns only on 'succeeded' at :199, so a buyer who re-opens /unlock?session_id would re-flip the row to succeeded) and user-dependent, not a guard; no money moves and no entitlement is lost, so the damage is silently understated creator earnings and platform revenue rather than a live security or payment failure.
evidence: Read BillingService.ts in full (markFailed :222-237, checkout metadata :161-162, grantFromSession :193-220, hasAccess :83-102, reconcileCheckout :269-282); stripe-webhook.controller.ts in full (:37-47 markFailed dispatch, :57-59 blanket 500); billing.controller.ts:149-172 (earnings status filter at :155); admin/v1/billing.controller.ts:15-26; 024_billing.sql (status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending' :24, no CHECK constraint on status, UNIQUE(user_id,content_type,content_id) :53); grep -rn markFailed repo-wide -> only the webhook caller plus the unrelated simulation RevisionService which does guard on expectedStatus; find services/billing/__tests__ -> grantFromSession.test.ts only, no markFailed or out-of-order coverage; grep registerStripeWebhookRoutes -> server.ts:571, unconditional. No Stripe API calls, no DB connections, no .env reads.

reason: Every refutation avenue closed. There the dedicated worker.ts:27-30 logs '[worker] failed to start' and process.exit(1), which under `restart: unless-stopped` is a visible crash loop, and deploy/scripts/health-check.sh:20 iterates the worker container. Residual real gap: a worker that started and later stops pulling — partly covered by boss.on('error') logging at pgBoss.ts:61. Worth keeping as a small hardening item, not a P1.

reason: Mechanism verified against the installed pg-boss 12.23.0, not memory: manager.js:1216-1229 createQueue builds plans.createQueue and executes it and nothing else; plans.js:565-568 emits `SELECT <schema>.create_queue(name, options::jsonb)`; the create_queue body inserts into <schema>.queue and ends `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (plans.js:492 partitioned form, :439 no-partitioning form) — no UPDATE, no error on an existing queue. updateQueue is a genuinely distinct UPDATE (manager.js:1260-1277 -> plans.js:678+) and `grep -rn 'updateQueue' backend-api/src` returns nothing. The per-call override route also fails: SendOptions is JobOptions & QueueOptions (types.d.ts:250) so retryLimit/expireInSeconds COULD be passed per send, but pgBossDriver.ts:30 passes only { singletonKey } and :54 passes only { localConcurrency }, so queue defaults are the only lever. No implicit sync exists either — getQueueCache (manager.js:471-483) throws 'Queue X does not exist' rather than creating one, and nothing in boss.js/contractor.js calls create_queue. pgBoss.ts:77-83 confirms both createQueue calls share one try and the catch logs at logger.debug while lib/logger.ts:4 defaults level to 'info', so the failure is invisible at default log level. BUT the first-creation-wins caveat lands: git shows crop's QUEUE_OPTIONS (retryLimit 3 / retryDelay 30 / retryBackoff true / expireInSeconds 1800 / deadLetter) are byte-identical to when the queue was introduced in 8afb6e9, and the video_generate queue is new in 1838bbf so it will be created fresh with correct options on the next boot. No deployed queue currently carries stale options, so the finding's 'if either queue was created before deadLetter was added, dead-lettering is not happening at all' is not true of this repo's history. The defect is real and the fix is right, but today it is a latent trap for the next options edit plus a debug-swallowed failure path, not a live misconfiguration — P2 rather than P1.

reason: The comment is not stale and no fix landed elsewhere. buildTierArgs (HLSTranscoder.ts:171-196) emits exactly `scale=W:H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=W:H:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2` with no squaring step and no setsar; grep for setsar|sample_aspect across services/video returns ZERO hits in non-test code. There is no pre-normalisation pass: runVideoTranscode.ts:38-58 downloads storage_key to source.<ext> and hands that raw path to transcodeToHLS, which loops TIERS and feeds the same untouched inputPath to buildTierArgs (HLSTranscoder.ts:422-441) — so the tier scale sees the source's storage dimensions, not its display dimensions. The gate really is geometry-blind: assertTierConformance (:286-321) checks (i) profile/level, (ii) first-frame keyframe, (iii) EXTINF durations, and nothing else — and a padded output is WxH by construction, so even a geometry check on frame size would pass while SAR stays wrong. ffmpegGraph.ts:7-9 and videoNormChain (:133-142) are the corrected chain, and the HLS real-encode suite's only fixtures are square-pixel lavfi sources (hlsTranscoder.realEncode.test.ts:73-83, 150-158), confirming no anamorphic coverage. ONE MECHANISM CORRECTION worth carrying into the report: vf_scale rewrites output SAR to preserve DAR, so the certain user-visible defect is pillarboxing plus a stream whose display size disagrees with the tier's declared RESOLUTION; the additional horizontal stretch appears only in players that ignore the container SAR, not universally. SEVERITY: reduced to P2 on reachability — playback is not broken (video still plays, just wrongly framed and wasting tier pixels), the export path (the headline deliverable) normalises correctly, and SAR != 1 is a minority of this product's sources: browser/screen recordings and modern phone video are square-pixel, leaving legacy DV/HDV/anamorphic-lens material as the affected population.

reason: The mechanic survives refutation, but the cost model is materially overstated. Mechanic: @fastify/multipart is registered exactly once (server.ts:198-200) with limits.fileSize = 10 GB, and none of the 9 non-test request.file()/toBuffer() sites passes a per-call limits, so toBuffer() (@fastify/multipart 8.3.1 index.js:370-395) pushes every chunk into fileChunks and only discards them once busboy flips file.truncated at the global limit - there is genuinely no pre-buffer cap. Four corrections, all mechanically checked. No other test covers abort -- grep ABORTED across every *.test.ts in backend-api/src returns exactly one hit, this test's own name, and the only sibling error-handling test (:190-201) covers LLM_ERROR. The comment does point at a real code path (ClaudeProvider.ts:117 `if (opts.abortSignal?.aborted) break;` returns partial content), but that does not rescue the test on two counts. (1) The contract the NAME asserts also genuinely exists: line 113 passes the signal into the SDK and 153-154 converts an SDK AbortError into AppError(ABORTED, 499) -- the mock at test:8-14 returns a hand-rolled async iterable that ignores the signal, so this test structurally CANNOT exercise the path it is named for. (2) The assertion is even weaker than the finding says: controller.abort() runs synchronously before the first microtask drains, so the aborted check breaks on the very first event and chunks stays empty -- result.content is '', not 'partial'. The test does not even demonstrate its own comment, and toBeDefined() would survive gutting the stream loop. Severity: real, but it is a test-hygiene item ranked above llm-011 (P2), the very defect it fails to catch, and above its own file's peers test-003..007 (untested money/auth paths) at P2.
